claim.quote: We identify neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at the 4.5$\sigma$ level of significance, by comparing diffuse emission models to a background-only hypothesis.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date. Published as Science 380, 6652, 1338-1343 (2023).

name: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane

significance.quote: We identify neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at the 4.5$\sigma$ level of significance, by comparing diffuse emission models to a background-only hypothesis.

summary.plain: Using machine learning on ten years of data, IceCube saw our own Milky Way glowing in neutrinos — the first picture of our galaxy made with particles instead of light.
summary.technical: Machine-learning cascade selection applied to ten years of IceCube data identifies diffuse Galactic-plane neutrino emission at 4.5σ against a background-only hypothesis; consistent with modelled diffuse emission but also compatible with unresolved point sources.

title: Observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Galactic plane
why_it_matters: First observation of neutrinos from the Milky Way, connecting Galactic cosmic rays to their interactions with interstellar matter.
